title: Watchy v1.5
tagline: An ESP32-S3 e-paper smartwatch someone actually fabricated: 86 footprints, two rails, a charger and a boost converter.

analyze.headline: 50 issues found, none serious. Worth a look before you order boards.

sections.title: Copper spacing (DRC)
sections.verdict: 50 issues found, none serious (worth a look).

findings.what: "+3V3" and "/32K_P" are very close but not quite touching at 1 location on the front copper layer (F.Cu) (tightest 0.154 mm, below your 0.200 mm rule).
findings.why: They are not shorted today, but at least one spot is below the spacing the board asks for. Small manufacturing variation, a solder smear, or contamination could bridge them, so it is a reliability risk rather than a guaranteed failure.
findings.fix: Open up the spacing between these two so the gap meets your clearance rule, or relax the rule deliberately if you know this spot is fine.

sections.title: Connectivity & wiring
sections.verdict: Looks healthy: no connectivity problems found.

sections.title: Signal integrity
sections.verdict: No signal-integrity failures, but 3 things worth a look (see below).

heads_up.what: A high-speed trace pair (DP / DN) is off its impedance target (W~0.150 mm, S~0.350 mm microstrip -> Zdiff ~ 146 ohm [target 90 ohm, USB differential]: estimate +62% from target).
heads_up.why: Fast links like USB (90 ohm differential) or Ethernet need their traces to present a specific impedance so the signal does not reflect off the wire and smear. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup; it is informational, not a confirmed failure, but a value well off target on a real high-speed net can make the link marginal or fail to enumerate.
heads_up.fix: If this pair is NOT a high-speed link (USB/Ethernet/HDMI), you can ignore it. If it is: adjust the trace width and pair spacing for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near the target (the formulas are in docs/checks/SI_CHECKS.md), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

heads_up.what: A high-speed trace pair (USB_D+ / USB_D-) is off its impedance target (W~0.150 mm, S~0.173 mm microstrip -> Zdiff ~ 125 ohm [target 90 ohm, USB differential]: estimate +39% from target).
heads_up.why: Fast links like USB (90 ohm differential) or Ethernet need their traces to present a specific impedance so the signal does not reflect off the wire and smear. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup; it is informational, not a confirmed failure, but a value well off target on a real high-speed net can make the link marginal or fail to enumerate.
heads_up.fix: If this pair is NOT a high-speed link (USB/Ethernet/HDMI), you can ignore it. If it is: adjust the trace width and pair spacing for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near the target (the formulas are in docs/checks/SI_CHECKS.md), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

heads_up.what: A single-ended trace (Net-(U4-LNA_IN/RF)) is off its impedance target (W~0.320 mm microstrip -> Z0 ~ 63 ohm [target 50 ohm, single-ended]: estimate +25% from target).
heads_up.why: A 50 ohm single-ended line is the convention for an RF or antenna feed: the trace has to present that impedance end to end or part of the signal reflects back instead of reaching the antenna, costing range and sensitivity. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup.
heads_up.fix: If this is not a controlled-impedance RF path, this estimate is informational. If it is: widen or narrow the trace for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near 50 ohm (the formulas are in docs/checks/SI_CHECKS.md), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

findings.what: "+3V3" and "/32K_P" are very close but not quite touching at 1 location on the front copper layer (F.Cu) (tightest 0.154 mm, below your 0.200 mm rule).
findings.why: They are not shorted today, but at least one spot is below the spacing the board asks for. Small manufacturing variation, a solder smear, or contamination could bridge them, so it is a reliability risk rather than a guaranteed failure.
findings.fix: Open up the spacing between these two so the gap meets your clearance rule, or relax the rule deliberately if you know this spot is fine.

sections.title: Connectivity & wiring
sections.verdict: Looks healthy: no connectivity problems found.

sections.title: Signal integrity
sections.verdict: No signal-integrity failures, but 3 things worth a look (see below).

heads_up.what: A high-speed trace pair (DP / DN) is off its impedance target (W~0.150 mm, S~0.350 mm microstrip -> Zdiff ~ 146 ohm [target 90 ohm, USB differential]: estimate +62% from target).
heads_up.why: Fast links like USB (90 ohm differential) or Ethernet need their traces to present a specific impedance so the signal does not reflect off the wire and smear. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup; it is informational, not a confirmed failure, but a value well off target on a real high-speed net can make the link marginal or fail to enumerate.
heads_up.fix: If this pair is NOT a high-speed link (USB/Ethernet/HDMI), you can ignore it. If it is: adjust the trace width and pair spacing for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near the target (the formulas are in docs/checks/SI_CHECKS.md), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

heads_up.what: A high-speed trace pair (USB_D+ / USB_D-) is off its impedance target (W~0.150 mm, S~0.173 mm microstrip -> Zdiff ~ 125 ohm [target 90 ohm, USB differential]: estimate +39% from target).
heads_up.why: Fast links like USB (90 ohm differential) or Ethernet need their traces to present a specific impedance so the signal does not reflect off the wire and smear. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup; it is informational, not a confirmed failure, but a value well off target on a real high-speed net can make the link marginal or fail to enumerate.
heads_up.fix: If this pair is NOT a high-speed link (USB/Ethernet/HDMI), you can ignore it. If it is: adjust the trace width and pair spacing for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near the target (the formulas are in docs/checks/SI_CHECKS.md), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

heads_up.what: A single-ended trace (Net-(U4-LNA_IN/RF)) is off its impedance target (W~0.320 mm microstrip -> Z0 ~ 63 ohm [target 50 ohm, single-ended]: estimate +25% from target).
heads_up.why: A 50 ohm single-ended line is the convention for an RF or antenna feed: the trace has to present that impedance end to end or part of the signal reflects back instead of reaching the antenna, costing range and sensitivity. This is a computed estimate, flagged only because the board did not formally declare a controlled-impedance stackup.
heads_up.fix: If this is not a controlled-impedance RF path, this estimate is informational. If it is: widen or narrow the trace for your actual layer stackup so the estimate lands near 50 ohm (the formulas are in docs/checks/SI_CHECKS.md), or ask your fab to build a controlled-impedance stackup to spec.

findings.what: Co-sim not available for this board.
findings.why: This board's MCU runs on an external emulator (Espressif QEMU). This quick report simulates only a 0.2 s window, and a chip like this one spends several simulated seconds in its boot ROM before your code starts, so the report would show a processor that has not booted yet. Running it long enough is a job of tens of wall-clock seconds, which is why it is not done inside a page load. The co-sim itself works, two ways: open the live sim ("Drive it live") to boot this firmware here in the app, or run it from a terminal, from the folder holding your files: "/Users/hauksbee-user/Tarski/Tarski-Repos/hauksbee-dev/target/release/hauksbee" run "watchy.kicad_pcb" --firmware "flash.bin" --headless
findings.fix: If the emulator is not installed yet, the Environment page installs it with one click.
